Young man--if you are going to act on one piece of advice from this thread, act on this one.

Take her out to dinner, then from there go to a movie that you both will enjoy. Don't pander to her and go straight for a chick-flick; don't pressure her into seeing some stupid dude movie.

During the film, casually place her hand in yours, or put your arm around her. If she responds to this during the movie by playing with your fingers or moving in closer, then ask her after the movie if she wants to come to your house and hang out, or watch another movie. Don't be forward or overly serious when asking--do it with a smile, like you would if you were asking a friend to hang out.

Post up on the couch after taking her jacket and offering her something to drink, and you'll be snuggling in no time. If your faces come close to one another and she seems comfortable, go in for the smooch. Make sure to pick a movie that would be a cute 'our first date/first kiss/ etc. movie.'

Make solid, gentle eye contact as long as you are speaking to one another--don't glance around or stare at your feet at all throughout the date. Practice good posture and good manners. Open doors for her (car doors included), but don't make it look like you are trying too hard. Do these things naturally, as if you really are just trying to make her night more enjoyable (because you should be!)

Relax, and if this goes well--you'll both have more fun at prom. It will be easier for you to chat, dance, and otherwise spend time with each other.

I promise you, with this route, you will not go wrong my friend. Good luck!

Priorities are important here. In other words - you're 17, and in high school a lot of people are just looking for a hook up or a string of hookups. If that's what you both want then it's usually not important what you do so long as you have a place to hang out and get close (in which case the movies are not so bad). However if you are both looking for a longer term relationship type thing then it matters a bit what you do. That doesn't mean over-think it though - really it means spending time doing something enjoyable where you can both relax, let loose a little bit and get to know each other to find common bonds. The important thing then is to be exactly who you are. If you try too hard to be something you think she wants you to be, but you aren't really that person normally, well eventually it's going to backfire. You don't want to be with someone who isn't for you nor do they want to be with someone who isn't for them. If it turns out you both are very different when getting to know each other then you move on, maybe become friends, maybe hit it and quit it. Best of luck.

Tang San is a master craftsman of hidden weapons who commits the ultimate sin of stealing sect secrets. Having reached the pinnacle of his art, he atones by suicide, but is reborn as the son of a simple blacksmith in a small mountain village in another world. In this world all children awaken their own Spirit at the age of six, and a rare few are born with spirit power, allowing them to cultivate their spirits to become Spirit Masters. Tang San is gifted with maximum innate spirit power, but his spirit is the standard for waste spirits, Blue Silver Grass. Will he be able to restore the brilliance of Tang Sect in this new world?

I enjoy how Factions is a bit more realistic than most shooters and was considering this related to a player's health. Do you think a gradual reduction in capability related to your health level would be better than the current up/down states? i.e. as you take more damage, your aim, movement speed, et cetera, decrease.

Also, how about all damage having an effect similar to the crossbow but at a much reduced rate. e.g. Each 9mm hit bleeds at .0008% per second until healed, each Semi-Auto Rifle hit bleed at .003% per second until healed, etc.

You could have certain threshold that, once passed, you cannot regain until a certain time period has passed (recovery) or a teammate with First Aid can heal you. Players at 1-40% health can only get back to 50%, 41-70% can heal to 80%, 70-99% can heal to 100% Kits can be more plentiful and a little faster to use. First Aid level X can bypass one level, level X+1 can always heal to 100%. I believe it would promote more teamwork.

On a side note, I think it would also be nice to have an Ammunition Specialist perk that gets "gift" ammo at every box or downed enemy. I think the game could use more class specialization, like healers and buffers etc.
